messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Sep 2025 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Trace-to-serve latency qualification — MagnoHealth follow-up

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we have alignment on how to validate p95/p99 end-to-end latency for MagnoHealth's inference path (hosted API vs your current provider):

What we heard you care about:
- p95 target: <= 120ms for simple prompt paths (normalized user queries)
- p99 target: <= 300ms for the same envelope (populated by burst traffic)
- Streaming: need server-sent partials for long-form outputs (token-level streaming) with ideal first-token <= 60ms
- Concurrency and throughput: baseline concurrency 40 req/s, peak burst up to 250 req/s for 30s windows
- Tracing: you want distributed traces for client->edge->model, and a sample of real traces to validate e2e timings

What Redwood will deliver for this validation:
1) A paired test plan (hosted Redwood API vs your incumbent) that runs the same traffic mix and replayed traces.
2) Measurement matrix (attached) that maps where time is spent (client, network, edge, model, post-process).
3) Stream probe for first-token timing and a streaming envelope test.
4) A short demo run and a reproducible script you can run in your environment.

Attachments: performance-matrix.csv (high-level measurement matrix), sample-traces-2000.jsonl (anonymized trace samples format).

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm which 2 production endpoints we should target and drop 10–20 representative traces into the Drive link below.
- Redwood (Jonas/Ben): run a paired run within 5 business days once traces are uploaded.
- Call: 30-min results sync to review p95/p99 and streaming delta. Suggested window: Tue or Wed next week.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-magnohealth-traces

If that looks right, we’ll schedule the probe and share an exact runbook.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful. Quick clarifications: 

1) Endpoints: please target the public inference endpoint (api.magnohealth.com/v1/complete) and our internal low-latency edge (edge-1.magnohealth.net).
2) Traces: I’ll drop 25 traces (mix of short prompts and long-form generation) into the Drive by EOD Monday — the traces include client-side timestamps and a short header for traffic mix.
3) Streaming: MagnoHealth expects partial tokens for the clinician-facing UI; first-token latency is critical because it drives perceived responsiveness.

A couple of asks from our side before you run:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood’s hosted run will add a proxy hop that materially affects p95 (we want to isolate model execution vs network and edge)?
- For the paired comparison, can you run one baseline with quantized model variants we currently use and one with your recommended configuration?

If we can get those answers in the next 24 hours we’ll lock in the traces and slot.

Thanks —
Sarah
Product Lead, MagnoHealth
sarah.kim@magnohealth.com

Sarah — great questions. Answers inline below and a small tweak to the runbook.

> Can you confirm whether Redwood’s hosted run will add a proxy hop that materially affects p95?
Yes — Redwood’s hosted option sits behind a thin edge proxy (regionally colocated), but the design goal is to minimize added hop latency. For the probe we will:
- Run three configurations for the hosted arm:
  A) Hosted (default edge proxy + curated kernel selection)
  B) Hosted (bypass-edge demo path — direct-to-inference for measurement)
  C) Hosted (bypass-edge + quantized model variant)
- Run two configurations for your incumbent: baseline and quantized variant (if available).
This will let us attribute time spent in network vs runtime.

> For the paired comparison, can you run one baseline with quantized model variants we currently use and one with your recommended configuration?
Yes — Jonas will coordinate quantization variants with your engineering contact. We will include model metadata in the matrix so p95/p99 comparisons are apples-to-apples.

Slight runbook tweak: please include 2 short synthetic bursts (30s @ 250 req/s) in addition to the replayed traces — that will stress tail behavior and streaming fairness.

Tentative schedule: Jonas and Ben will kick off runs Tue morning PT once the traces are in the Drive. I’ll send an invite for Wed 09:00 PT to review results (30 min).

—
Marissa
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 09:08:00 -07:00
To: platform@magnohealth.com
Subject: Run commands + stream probe details

Sarah / Magno infra team —

Two things for the run:
1) Stream probe: we’ll measure first-token across three regimes (idle, steady-state @40 rps, burst @250 rps). Probe uses token-level SSE and timestamps on both client and server side.
2) Replayer: we’ll replay traces with the following flags:
   - concurrency=40
   - peak-burst-schedule: 30s ramp-to-250, hold 30s, decay 15s
   - inject-network-latency=0–10ms (to mimic your edge hops)

Command (example):
./replay --traces sample-traces-2000.jsonl --concurrency 40 --burst 250 --burst-duration 30 --stream-probe --out metrics-magnohosted.csv

We’ll also capture distributed traces (Zipkin headers) and a per-request timing breakdown to populate the attached performance-matrix. If you have an allowlist for incoming test IPs, we’ll add our runner IPs once you confirm.

— end forwarded —

Ben
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
